correctness.rationale: A white set is skew-stalled exactly when no vertex has one white neighbor. For a book graph, the degree-two page vertices force the membership equivalences y_i in W iff a in W and x_i in W iff b in W, so the only nonempty stalled sets are the two bipartition classes and the whole graph. Therefore an initial set skew forces exactly when it hits both classes. Independent brute-force simulation checks every subset for n=1 through 8, all 96 polynomial coefficients, the minimum size and multiplicity, and the failed number.

value.rationale: Book graphs are a standard infinite Cartesian-product family. The result gives a complete all-initial-set classification, a closed forcing polynomial, every minimum set, and the maximum failed size from one structural theorem. The two-class hitting description exposes a natural bipartite mechanism and is materially stronger than a scalar parameter computation or an arbitrary finite slice.
